answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, non-reusable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when an arbitrated fraud claim is upheld. Splitting one identity into a grove of aliases does not multiply the attacker’s resources: every alias must tie up capital, and each fraudulent action risks losing it. A glacier-slow withdrawal delay keeps stake exposed during disputes, while lotus-style account names add no trust; the defense is the costly collateral, not the identities.
